newsitem.title: USA: US Texas power mostly steady amid moderate weather.
newsitem.headline: US Texas power mostly steady amid moderate weather.

text.p: Wholesale power prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) were mostly unchanged Friday amid a wide range of price discussion, as temperatures were expected to be near-normal through the weekend, market sources said.

Prices for peak, firm power for weekend and Monday deliveries were talked around $26.00 per Megawatt hour (MWh), with some deals reported done as high as $28.00. This is compared with the $25.00-26.50 range evident on Thursday.
Off-peak ERCOT power for weekend delivery was seen around $15.00.
December peak power was talked steady at $24.25-24.75, while January/February ERCOT power prices hovered in the $24.50-25.50 range, sources said.
Texas Utilities' 1,150 megawatt Comanche Peak unit 1 in Glen Rose, Texas, is expected to restart Monday following its refueling and maintenance outage, according to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission.
